P0: LEAKY-ABSTRACTION; field overloads two meanings with no written contract; HasParent reflexivity/strictness unspecified (P1)

P1: WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE; conflates 'is root' with 'which namespace owns it' in one nilable pointer

P0: LSP violation; subtype satisfies type but not contract; must panic, error, or be feature-flagged

issues.description: ACL.root changed from bool to *namespace.Namespace with unverified HasParent semantics and unstated invariant
issues.detail: The authorization fast-path now reads `if !ns.HasParent(a.root) { return ret }` then grants RootPrivs. Correctness hinges on the direction and reflexivity of HasParent (does N have itself as parent? is it strict-ancestor or ancestor-or-self?), neither of which is stated at the call site nor exercised by the test. The single test covers ns1==a.root and a negative (child-root acting from root) but not grandchild/sibling/root-policy-from-child cases. The field also overloads 'is root policy' + 'which namespace owns it' into a nullable pointer; readers must know that nil means not-root. Capture rootNamespaceID/path as values, or decompose into explicit fields (isRoot bool + rootNamespace *Namespace), and state the invariant.

issues.description: Core.NamespaceSealed is a stub that unconditionally returns false while consumers already gate on it
issues.detail: The new method has a TODO and returns false in every case, but ListAllNamespaces and root-token paths are already wired to consult it. This ships a security-adjacent surface change with enforcement turned off and no compile-time signal forcing the SealManager PR to wire it in. The doc comment ('direct ancestry line') also disagrees with the name (suggesting 'this exact namespace'). Mitigations: gate behind a feature flag/build tag, return an error/panic for paths that materially depend on the answer, or hold the consumer migration until SealManager lands. As written, the negative branch can never be exercised and downstream PRs may regress silently.

issues.description: NewACL drops the 'root policy only in root namespace' invariant without a stated replacement gate
issues.detail: Previously NewACL rejected a root-named policy attached in any non-root namespace. The diff removes that guard and stores the context ns as a.root, effectively letting any ACL constructed with a root policy under any ns context grant root within that subtree. The PR does not enumerate NewACL call sites nor exhibit a proof that all callers are authorized to mint root policies at the ns they pass. The compensating check (presumably in a not-yet-landed SealManager / token generator) is not in the diff. Either show all callers preserve the invariant, restore the guard, or state the new precondition explicitly on NewACL.

issues.description: AdjustErrorStatusCode if-chain to switch refactor silently changes precedence semantics
issues.detail: The old code was a sequence of independent if-statements where multiple could fire and the HTTPCoded branch could override earlier writes. The new switch returns on the first matching case, so an error that both wraps ErrSealed and implements HTTPCodedError now locks in 503 and never reaches the HTTPCoded branch. This is a behavior change disguised as a stylistic cleanup. Either restore the independent-ifs form, document the new precedence with a test, or express the intent as a slice of (predicate, statusFn) applied in order.

issues.description: errwrap.Contains string-matching on ErrNamespaceSealed message is fragile sentinel detection
issues.detail: `errwrap.Contains(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed.Error())` matches by substring of the error message ('namespace is sealed'), which is short, generic, and the wrong way to identify a sentinel. Any wrapped error whose message happens to contain that substring will be downgraded to 503. Adding a second sealed-error sentinel doubles the risk that one message becomes a substring of another. Prefer `errors.Is(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed)` (and the same for ErrSealed) with wrap-chain `%w`.

issues.description: ListAllNamespaces contract change (now includes sealed namespaces) is not reflected at call sites
issues.detail: Four call sites in core.go/core_metrics.go/counters.go switched from `c.namespaceStore.ListAllNamespaces(ctx, true)` to `c.ListNamespaces(ctx)`, hiding the include-sealed boolean inside the wrapper. The semantic delta matters per-caller: MFA configs and locked-user updates probably should NOT iterate sealed namespaces, while entity gauges and active-token counts probably should. The PR does not justify the choice per call site, the new contract is not written down on the method, and the boolean parameter has vanished from local reasoning.

issues.description: Patch bundles three unrelated changes — split into separate commits
issues.detail: (1) ACL root-namespace semantics refactor (load-bearing); (2) ErrNamespaceSealed sentinel + Core.NamespaceSealed stub + ListAllNamespaces wiring; (3) mass test-context rewrites from context.Background() to namespace.RootContext(t.Context()). Mashed together, the test churn obscures the four lines in acl.go that actually change security behavior. Splitting would make `git log -p` and future bisection tractable.

issues.description: AllowOperation reordering of namespace.FromContext vs root fast-path changes failure mode on missing-namespace contexts
issues.detail: Previously a.root was consulted before namespace.FromContext; now FromContext runs first, so a context with no namespace yields default-deny before any root short-circuit. For root tokens this is a tightening, and may be intended, but the new contract on missing-namespace context (deny vs allow-if-root) is not stated. State the contract explicitly.

issues.description: NSTokenLength = TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID is cryptic and arithmetically suspect
issues.detail: The expression `"."[1]` indexes past the end of a one-byte string — in Go this is a compile-time bounds error for a literal, or a runtime issue elsewhere; the author likely meant `len(".")` (=1). Even granting that, the constant smuggles token structure (`<token>.<nsID>`) into an arithmetic formula. The right primitive is a codec: an encode function and a decode function returning (token, nsID, error), with the length derived from those. Either way, reconcile description with code, name the separator (`NSTokenSeparator = '.'`), and use `TokenLen + 1 + NamespaceIDLen` or equivalent.

issues.description: leaseView / tokenIndexView unification removes root-namespace special case without proving byte-identical storage paths
issues.detail: Previously these methods branched on `ns.ID == RootNamespaceID`, using systemBarrierView.SubView(...) for root and namespaceMountEntryView(...) for child namespaces. The diff unifies both into `NamespaceView(m.core.barrier, ns).SubView(...)`. For this to be a true refactor, `NamespaceView(barrier, RootNamespace).SubView(prefix)` must produce byte-identical storage keys to the prior path; otherwise existing root-namespace leases become unreadable post-upgrade. Add a migration test or assertion, or a one-line invariant comment establishing equivalence.

issues.description: ACL.root field comment is imprecise and contradicts the field name
issues.detail: The comment reads 'root property is a non-nil namespace if the "root" named policy (and only "root") is present.' The field is a `*namespace.Namespace`, not 'a non-nil namespace', and '(and only "root")' is not reflected in the type. A precise comment: 'root is non-nil iff the policy set consists of exactly one policy named "root"; when non-nil it identifies the namespace in which that policy was instantiated.' Even better, rename the field (e.g. `rootNamespace`/`rootPolicyNS`) so the comment becomes unnecessary.

issues.description: response_util switch pre-declares an hce sentinel whose purpose is non-obvious
issues.detail: `var hce HTTPCodedError = &codedError{}` is now declared above the switch purely so `errwrap.ContainsType(err, hce)` can reference it. A reader who has not seen the old code will not understand why an empty `codedError` is constructed. Inline the type identity (e.g. `(*codedError)(nil)`) or add a one-line comment naming it as a type-identity sentinel for ContainsType/GetType.

issues.description: Wholesale inlining of namespaceMountEntryView pushes barrier choice and prefix string to every call site
issues.detail: Removing `namespaceMountEntryView` and inlining `NamespaceView(c.barrier, ns).SubView(prefix)` at each caller means every site must know which barrier to use and the full prefix string. If transparency is the goal, define small named view constructors (e.g. `passwordPolicyView(core, ns)`) so the prefix is not repeated; otherwise expect drift.

issues.description: Mechanical context.Background() -> namespace.RootContext(...) test churn signals ambient-context coupling
issues.detail: Dozens of test sites are rewritten because functions now require a namespace in context — a value passed through an identity channel. Each function could take `ns *Namespace` as an explicit parameter; the current direction doubles down on context-as-grab-bag. Worth a hammock before the pattern calcifies. Pike notes the same churn could at least be reduced via a `testRootCtx(t)` helper to shrink the diff.

synthesis.summary: The panel is unusually unanimous on two load-bearing P0s: (1) ACL.root flipped from bool to *namespace.Namespace with an unverified HasParent fast-path and an unstated invariant — all six reviewers flag it, and Torvalds, Dijkstra, Hickey, and Liskov rate it P0 because the test only covers same-namespace cases and never exercises sibling/cousin/grandchild/root-from-child paths where ancestry semantics decide the security property; (2) Core.NamespaceSealed is a stub that unconditionally returns false while ListAllNamespaces and root-token paths already consult it — Torvalds, Hickey, Liskov, and Dijkstra all label this 'lying scaffolding' and demand either a feature flag, an error-return contract, or holding the consumer migration until SealManager lands. Hickey, Liskov, and Dijkstra additionally raise a P0 about NewACL dropping the 'root policy only in root namespace' invariant with no stated replacement gate. The strongest preserved disagreement is on AdjustErrorStatusCode's if-chain-to-switch refactor: Hickey, Torvalds, Pike, and Dijkstra independently call out a silent precedence change (first-match-wins now suppresses the HTTPCoded passthrough), while Knuth treats the refactor as a readability win and only flags a minor sentinel-variable clarity issue — the panel splits on whether this is a behavior bug or merely a cleanup. Secondary unanimity: the NSTokenLength `TokenLen + \".\"[1] + nsID` formula is flagged as cryptic-or-wrong by every reviewer, and errwrap.Contains substring-matching on ErrNamespaceSealed is universally criticized as fragile vs errors.Is.
